extracted.intended_audience: fans of Saturday Night Live and readers interested in TV production / aspiring comedy writers and TV crew
extracted.subtask_description: Describes the end-to-end process and practical requirements for mounting a new episode of a weekly live sketch-comedy show (Saturday Night Live), from pitching and writing through build, rehearsal, dress and live broadcast. Emphasizes time pressure, collaboration with departments, host-specific tailoring, and live-audience testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fit to host's voice and strengths
rubrics_metrics.description: Sketches must work with the guest host's unique flavor; writing must be adjusted to what the host does well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "Each host has such a different voice... Writing for Kevin Hart is a whole lot different than writing for Blake Shelton, and you have to adjust your style to fit what they do well."

rubrics_metrics.name: Host buy-in vs. institutional knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: The host often has strong views or attachments to material, but producers (especially Lorne Michaels) will balance host preferences against what 'knows the room' and what will actually work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "Sometimes, if a host is really attached [to a sketch or a joke], I will make the case as to why I don't think it's going to work, but … you can't explain that we know the room better than they do."

rubrics_metrics.name: Speed and deadline adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: Sketches and pages must be written and turned around on extremely tight deadlines (e.g., sketches due at noon for a Wednesday table read), often requiring overnight writing sessions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "With sketches due at noon the next day for Wednesday evening's table read, an all-night writing session commences... I usually get there Tuesday at 1 p.m. and we write to about noon on Wednesday so almost a full 24 hours."

rubrics_metrics.name: Stand-out humor at table read
rubrics_metrics.description: To advance past the table read, material must register strongly in a long read-through environment; being 'pretty funny' is required to break through fatigue and skepticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "From there, it's on to the read-through... The process has been known to take up to three hours. 'Everyone is tired and grumpy,' Tucker quipped. 'You've got to be pretty funny to get everybody going.'"

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive selection (winners and losers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each week's sketches compete for limited slots; selection is a 'friendly, respectful competition' judged by Michaels, producers and head writers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "Every week there are winners and losers, and so it's a friendly, respectful competition... if a writer's sketch is deemed worthy enough to advance, they spend Wednesday evening meeting with the heads of the costume, make-up, set design and special effect departments..."

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility with design and technical departments
rubrics_metrics.description: Selected sketches must be feasible for costume, make-up, set design, and special effects — writers meet department heads to share vision and learn what will actually work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "If a writer's sketch is deemed worthy enough to advance, they spend Wednesday evening meeting with the heads of the costume, make-up, set design and special effect departments to share their vision for the sketch, hear what will actually work..."

rubrics_metrics.name: Set-buildability under time constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets must be constructible quickly (often starting Thursday morning) and multiple sets (upwards of 13) must be completed in a very short window.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "At 6 a.m. on Thursday morning... Eugene Lee and his team get to work on constructing the sets... With time limited and upwards of 13 sets to be built... 'You have to spend what you have to spend.'"

rubrics_metrics.name: Costume, wig and make-up readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Costumes, wigs and make-up need to be designed and prepared on the Thursday–Friday timeline so they're available for blocking, rehearsals and dress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "Meanwhile, back at 30 Rock, costumes, wigs and make-up are starting to be designed as director Don Roy King steps in to begin blocking and rehearsals..."

rubrics_metrics.name: Blockability and rehearsability
rubrics_metrics.description: Sketches must be blockable and able to be rehearsed effectively by the director and cast within the limited rehearsal period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "Don Roy King steps in to begin blocking and rehearsals with cast and crew... 'For our Saturday run-through, we have one shot.'"

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-taped sketch production and turnaround
rubrics_metrics.description: Any pre-taped sketches must be filmed (often Friday) and edited overnight so they're ready for inclusion in the live show.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "Blocking and rehearsals continue into Friday. And any pre-taped sketch? It's filmed that day, too, with editing happening overnight."

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete-elements Saturday run-through
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a critical 1 p.m. Saturday run-through where all elements (sets, costumes, props) must come together; it's often the first time everything exists together and there's only one shot to get it right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "Ultimately, it all has to come together on Saturday at 1 o'clock with all its elements... 'For our Saturday run-through, we have one shot.'"

rubrics_metrics.name: Live dress rehearsal audience testing
rubrics_metrics.description: An 8 p.m. live dress rehearsal before an audience is used to gauge what works; Lorne uses audience reaction to trim or reorder material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "At 8 p.m., before a live audience, the entire show is performed as if it were the real thing... Michaels uses the reaction from the fresh set of eyes in Studio 8H to decide what goes as he trims the fat once more."

rubrics_metrics.name: Runtime and timing discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The show must be tightly timed to fit the 90-minute/airtime constraints; timing is monitored closely and sketches may be cut or shortened to hit the mark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "But just because it's finally showtime doesn't mean the work is over... 'there is that sense of potential panic throughout the 90 minutes,' he admitted... time is watched like a hawk."

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility to accept last-minute cuts and reordering
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers and performers must accept that sketches can be thrown out, reordered, or heavily cut—even large swaths removed—right up to showtime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "Lorne will throw out two or three sketches entirely, reorder the rest of the show... With King making cuts on the fly—not just a line here or there, but often gutting sketches of large swaths of material..."

rubrics_metrics.name: One-shot pressure in run-through
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain rehearsals (e.g., the Saturday run-through) offer a single chance to get staging and timing right, so segments must be prepared to succeed on one attempt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "'For our Saturday run-through, we have one shot,' DeVito added. 'One shot to get it right. One shot with costumes, one shot with sets, with props, with everything.'"

rubrics_metrics.name: Stamina and sustained effort
rubrics_metrics.description: Mounting a weekly live show requires intense, sustained effort and personal stamina from cast, writers and crew, with long hours and minimal days off.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "Each week, the six-day work schedule begins on Monday... all of whom have only had one day off since the last show... 'You write all night... I usually stay all night and write straight through.'"

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration with musical guest logistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Musical guests must be scheduled, rehearse on-site, shoot promos with the host and participate in photo cards and other cross-show elements; their timing must be coordinated into the production week.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "Thursday also marks the first day that the week's musical guests arrive on set to begin their rehearsals. That afternoon, they'll shoot their promo with the host... before they and the host pose for those iconic photo cards..."
